sources.name: ArchDaily
sources.summary: The spatial consequences of urban form are revealed when health outcomes are mapped over neighborhoods . Neighborhoods that support walking, daily errands, social interaction, and access to essential services create opportunities to incorporate physical activity into routine tasks. Places that are organized around long distances and automobile travel suppress this opportunity . Physical activity and the motivation to incorporate it into daily life are shaped by the distance to a grocery store, the safety of a pedestrian crossing, the frequency of public transportation, the width of a sidewalk , and the quantity of services within walking distance.
